facts.business: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is an Indian public sector engineering and manufacturing company engaged in the design, engineering, construction, testing, commissioning, and servicing of a wide range of products and services for the core sectors of the economy, primarily power generation (thermal, hydro, nuclear, gas, solar), transmission, industry, transportation, defence, and oil & gas.

guidance_or_targets.statement: Policy makers have envisaged thermal capacity of 315 GW by 2035-36 as per Long Term Resource Adequacy Plan (LTRAP) released by CEA.
Government of India's roadmap for expanding country's nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047.
CEA's roadmap targeting 100 GW of Pumped Storage Projects (PSP) capacity by 2035-36.
India's NDC target of achieving 60% cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources by 2035.

auditor.name: Statutory Auditors (names not specified in excerpts)
auditor.emphasis_or_qualification: Unmodified opinion on the adequacy and operating effectiveness of the Company's Internal Financial Controls over financial reporting.

key_risks: Geopolitical tensions and trade frictions impacting global economy
Foreign currency exchange rate risk (USD, Euro, others) affecting profit/loss
Execution risk in large EPC projects
Technology transition risk with shift towards non-fossil fuel based energy
Dependence on government policy for thermal power ordering
Concentration risk with major customers (CPSUs, Adani Group)
facts.related_party_note: Major customers include CPSUs (Central Public Sector Undertakings) with revenue of Rs 14,233.40 Crore and Adani Group with revenue of Rs 6,672.58 Crore in FY 2025-26. Joint Ventures include BHEL-GE Gas Turbine Services Private Limited, NTPC-BHEL Power Projects Private Limited, Raichur Power Corporation Limited, and Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd.
